ingredient_evidence.claim: A 2007 cosmetic-science study evaluated octyldodecanol in stick formulations for sensory properties and skin-care use; it provides formulation-use evidence but not a specific facial skin-type effect.
ingredient_evidence.source_name: Gámbaro et al., Journal of Cosmetic Science (2006)

ingredient_evidence.claim: 2025 case report documented allergic contact dermatitis to octyldodecanol in a men's anti-aging cream; this establishes a reported sensitization signal but does not determine general facial-skin compatibility or prevalence.
AAD lists glycerin among facial-mask ingredients for dry or sensitive skin; clinical studies also report improved hydration with topical glycerol in dry skin.
ingredient_evidence.citation: Do facial masks work...; Effects of Locally Applied Glycerol... (PMID 27349297)

ingredient_evidence.claim: Niacinamide/niacin safety assessment found no significant skin irritation, sensitization, or photosensitization at tested cosmetic-use levels.
ingredient_evidence.source_name: Final report on niacinamide and niacin

ingredient_evidence.claim: Topical niacinamide has clinical evidence for skin barrier support and dermatologic uses including acne.

A case report documented allergic contact dermatitis involving rosemary leaf extract in a cleansing gel, with a positive patch test to the extract. This supports retaining a sensitization-risk evidence record separately from facial-scope classification.

Topical rosemary applications are documented in a review covering cosmetic formulations and dermatologic/topical uses, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory applications; the review also notes the need for stronger clinical evidence.

Topical olive oil has been studied on human skin; a 2012 study found reduced stratum-corneum integrity and mild erythema after 4 weeks, including in volunteers with atopic dermatitis. This is safety/skin-barrier evidence, not a basis to classify the ingredient as incompatible with a skin type by itself.

Facial skincare use is documented in a 2023 clinical study of clay-mask formulations containing Olea europaea fruit oil applied to adult women's facial skin; the study evaluated moisture, oiliness, texture, pigmentation, sensitivity and wrinkles. The study tested the oil both alone and in combination, so effects cannot be attributed exclusively to the oil.
Benzyl alcohol can cause allergic contact dermatitis, particularly with prolonged/repeated exposure.
ingredient_evidence.source_name: Benzyl Alcohol: Allergen of the Year 2026

ingredient_risks.note: Benzyl alcohol can cause allergic contact dermatitis; published reviews/case evidence support a sensitization signal, while safety assessments also indicate generally safe cosmetic use under specified conditions.

Allergic contact dermatitis has been reported for octyldodecanol in cosmetic/topical products, including a 2025 case report. This is a risk signal, not evidence of incompatibility with a particular skin type.
A published case report documented allergic contact dermatitis to rosemary leaf extract in a cleansing gel with positive patch testing to the extract.
Retinoid ester (vitamin A derivative). Retinoids are generally advised to be avoided during pregnancy as a precaution.
Rated highly comedogenic in rabbit-ear comedogenicity testing; may clog pores in acne-prone skin.
Plant oil rich in C12–C24 fatty acids/triglycerides that Malassezia yeast can use for growth; may aggravate Malassezia (fungal) folliculitis.
Polysorbates (Tweens) are fatty acid esters used to culture Malassezia in the lab; may support Malassezia growth on skin.
